Vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) arises from the vestibular nerve in the internal auditory canal and grows toward the cerebellopontine angle: "ice cream cone" shape, intense enhancement, often cystic areas. Meningioma, by contrast, has a broad dural base, a dural tail, and rarely enters the canal.
The Koos classification guides the choice: 1 intracanalicular only; 2 in the angle without contact with the brainstem; 3 in contact with the brainstem without displacing it; 4 with brainstem compression. Small lesions are kept under surveillance: growth (usually > 2 mm/year or a 20% increase in volume) leads to radiosurgery or surgery.
In the comparison, always measure in the same way in both exams, preferably using volume: diameter underestimates growth of irregular lesions.
